message.content: One of the most celebrated sculptures that emerged in the 19th‑century canon is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889).  Rodin’s bronze, depicting an intimate embrace, became an icon of modern sculpture and is often cited alongside his later masterpiece “The Thinker” as defining works of the era.  While “The Thinker” itself was cast in 1902, Rodin’s influence began in the late 1800s, making “The Kiss” a quintessential 19th‑century sculpture.
